title: Enterprise cost proposal triage protocol for commitments, invoicing, and marketplace credits
creator: Ariana Chen
description: Problem: Enterprise teams submit a wide range of non-bug requests related to pricing, committed usage, invoice adjustments, marketplace payouts and crediting. Current intake is ad-hoc, leading to slow response times, inconsistent decisions, and revenue leakage risk. Purpose: define a repeatable, observable triage protocol for pricing/packaging/billing requests that clarifies routing, scoring, SLA, and next-step templates so PM, Sales/RevOps, Finance, and Eng can make timely, auditable decisions. Scope: commitments (reserved capacity/discounts), invoice disputes & adjustments, cost allocation/chargeback tagging, and marketplace seller credits/fees. Out of scope: technical billing system refactors and tax/regulatory consulting which will be separate engineering/finance projects.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Intake form + auto-score launched and used by Sales/CS for new requests; 2) Routing rules implemented in intake workflow that route to RevOps/Finance/PM within SLA; 3) Decision templates (approve/reject/needs-more-info) available and used; 4) Audit log entries created for all final decisions and stored for 1 year; 5) Pilot with two enterprise customers (one commitment, one marketplace credit) completed and retro documented
steps_workflow: 1) Intake: standardized form in Zendesk/Drive with required fields (customer ARR, request type, requested financial delta, contract link, urgency rationale, supporting docs)
2) Auto-scoring: algorithmic score computed from fields (financial_impact, contract_presence, legal_required, customer_tier) producing A/B/C triage buckets
3) Routing: Bucket A -> RevOps + Finance immediate review; Bucket B -> PM + Sales review; Bucket C -> PM backlog with templated response
4) Decision templates: use pre-approved responses and negotiation guardrails (min/max discount %, credit caps, timeline constraints)
5) Escalation: if score predicts >$50k revenue delta or legal required -> automatically escalate to Director of RevOps and Legal
6) Verification: Finance records invoice adjustments and generates audit entry; PM owns post-decision customer communication templates
7) Close loop: log resolution, tag original ticket with release/feature implications, and schedule root-cause follow-up if recurring

decisions: Adopt auto-score buckets (A/B/C) — score metric includes financial_impact, contract_link, customer_tier, and legal_flag
Finance requires hard cap on manager-level approvals: <= $25k or <=3% MRR. Anything above routes to Director-level and Legal where applicable
SLA targets agreed: Bucket A - 48 hours initial response; Bucket B - 5 business days; Bucket C - next planning cycle
Audit log retention default set to 12 months; Security to validate retention for EU customers
Intake form will live in Zendesk with GitHub webhook to create a PM ticket when 'approved for PM' is selected
tradeoffs_and_risks: Speed vs. control: Lowering approval thresholds speeds customer outcomes but increases financial risk; Finance suggested conservative caps for pilot
Tooling complexity: Full integration with billing ledger is higher effort (ENG-8421) vs. a manual Finance queue approach. Chosen: phased approach starting manual + lightweight automation
Auditability vs. privacy: storing supporting documents in S3 aids review but requires PII cleansing and EU data considerations
Customer experience: templated responses reduce time but need personalization to avoid churn; include customizable fields for Sales
